draftA:
REQ-1 Trigger: send a delay notification when the carrier's latest ETA is more than 2 hours after the promised delivery time; a gap of exactly 2 hours or less does not trigger.
REQ-2 Source of truth is the carrier's latest ETA, received in UTC; compare it to the promised time on a common UTC basis.
REQ-3 Every time shown to the customer (promised time and new estimate) is rendered in the delivery address's local time.
REQ-4 At most two notifications per shipment: the first on the initial breach, and a second only if the estimate slips a further 2 hours beyond the ETA used in the first notification (requester did not say whether exactly 2 hours counts here; assumed 2 hours or more, unlike REQ-1's strict "more than").
AC-1 Promised 2024-06-10 15:00 local at a New York address (UTC-4) = 19:00 UTC; carrier ETA 21:30 UTC is 2h30m late, so notify, showing new estimate 17:30 local on 2024-06-10.
AC-2 Same shipment, carrier ETA 21:00 UTC is exactly 2h late: no notification sent.
AC-3 After the AC-1 notification (ETA 21:30 UTC), a new ETA of 23:30 UTC is a 2-hour further slip: send the second notification showing 19:30 local; shipment has now had 2 notifications and no more are sent.
AC-4 After the AC-1 notification, a new ETA of 23:00 UTC is only a 1h30m slip: no second notification, even though it is 4 hours past the promised time.
draftB:
REQ-1: Notify the customer when the carrier's latest ETA is more than 2 hours after the promised delivery time.
REQ-2: Use only the carrier's latest ETA, which arrives in UTC, for that check.
REQ-3: Show times in the delivery address's local time.
REQ-4: Send one notification per shipment, plus one more only if a new ETA slips by a further 2 hours, and send no third.
AC-1: Promised 14:00 local and ETA 16:00 local: no notice. ETA 16:01 local: send the first notice.
AC-2: ETA 18:01 UTC at a UTC-4 delivery address is 14:01 local; against promised 12:00 local that is 2 hours 1 minute late, so notify and show 14:01 local.
AC-3: After a notice for ETA 17:00 local, ETA 18:59 local sends nothing; ETA 19:00 local sends the one extra notice; any later slip sends none.

findings.title: Exact further-slip boundary assumed
findings.detail: Requester said a further 2-hour slip may trigger a second notice but did not say if exactly 2 hours counts. The draft assumes 2 hours or more, and AC-3 sends on an exact 2-hour slip, unlike the stated more-than rule.
findings.quote: requester did not say whether exactly 2 hours counts here; assumed 2 hours or more, unlike REQ-1's strict "more than"

reviewOfA.strengths: The acceptance checks correctly convert 15:00 New York time on 2024-06-10 to 19:00 UTC and keep the first notice strictly more than 2 hours late.

findings.title: Second-notice threshold inconsistent with first
findings.detail: The first notice requires strictly more than 2 hours late (16:00 exactly sends nothing), but the second fires at exactly a 2-hour further slip (17:00 to 19:00). Pick one convention or state explicitly that the second trigger is inclusive.
findings.quote: ETA 19:00 local sends the one extra notice

findings.title: Conversion rule stated only in example
findings.detail: The ETA arrives in UTC but promised times are local. Only AC-2 shows the conversion; no requirement states that the UTC ETA must be converted to the delivery address's local time before the lateness comparison, leaving AC-1's "ETA 16:00 local" unexplained.
findings.quote: REQ-2: Use only the carrier's latest ETA, which arrives in UTC, for that check.

reviewOfB.strengths: AC-2's arithmetic is correct and well chosen: 18:01 UTC at a UTC-4 address is 14:01 local, 2 hours 1 minute past a 12:00 promise, and the notice shows the local time as required.

merge.document:
REQ-1 Trigger: send a delay notification when the carrier's latest ETA is more than 2 hours after the promised delivery time; a gap of exactly 2 hours or less does not trigger.
REQ-2 Source of truth is the carrier's latest ETA only, received in UTC.
REQ-3 Comparison: convert the promised time and the ETA to a common basis (UTC) before measuring lateness, since the ETA arrives in UTC and the promised time is local.
REQ-4 Display: every time shown to the customer (promised time and new estimate) is rendered in the delivery address's local time.
REQ-5 Count: at most two notifications per shipment. The first on the initial breach; the second only if a new ETA is more than 2 hours later than the ETA used in the first notification. No third notification. (The requester did not state the exact boundary for the further slip; it is aligned with REQ-1's strict "more than".)
AC-1 Promised 2024-06-10 15:00 local at a New York address (UTC-4) = 19:00 UTC; carrier ETA 21:30 UTC is 2h30m late, so notify, showing new estimate 17:30 local on 2024-06-10.
AC-2 Same shipment, carrier ETA 21:00 UTC is exactly 2h late: no notification.
AC-3 After the AC-1 notification (ETA 21:30 UTC), a new ETA of 23:30 UTC is a further slip of exactly 2h: no second notification.
AC-4 After the AC-1 notification, a new ETA of 23:31 UTC is a 2h01m further slip: send the second notification showing 19:31 local; no further notifications for this shipment.
AC-5 After the AC-1 notification, a new ETA of 23:00 UTC is only a 1h30m slip: no second notification, even though it is 4 hours past the promised time.
AC-6 Promised 12:00 local at a UTC-4 delivery address; ETA 18:01 UTC = 14:01 local, 2h01m late: notify and show 14:01 local.
merge.keptFromA: Draft A's structure, its explicit strict "more than 2 hours" boundary with the worked New York example (15:00 local = 19:00 UTC, ETA 21:30 UTC), and its cases distinguishing a real further slip from one that is still late but under 2 hours.
merge.keptFromB: Draft B's clear two-notice cap wording and its UTC-to-local conversion check (18:01 UTC at a UTC-4 address = 14:01 local against a 12:00 promise), kept as AC-6.

resolutions.note: The second notification now requires more than 2 hours of further slip, matching REQ-1; AC-3 shows an exact 2h slip sending nothing and AC-4 shows 2h01m sending the second notice. The assumption is stated in REQ-5 because the requester did not define the boundary.

resolutions.finding: D-B1 Second-notice threshold inconsistent with first
resolutions.note: Same issue as D-A1: one strict more-than convention is now used for both triggers, with AC-3 and AC-4 testing each side of the boundary.

resolutions.finding: D-B2 Conversion rule stated only in example
resolutions.note: REQ-3 now requires converting the UTC ETA and the local promised time to a common UTC basis before comparing, and REQ-4 keeps display in the delivery address's local time; draft B's local-only AC-1 was replaced by cases that state both the UTC ETA and the local display.
